Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

hesitate verb

also hesitation, hesitant, don’t hesitate, without hesitation, hang back, waver, be in two minds

classical

Cic. Sen. 25: nec vērō dubitat agricola … respondēre
Caes. B.G. 2.23.2 (Lewis & Short)

dubitō, dubitāre, dubitāvī, dubitātum

verb, first conjugation, with the infinitive

hesitate (to do something)

With an infinitive dubitāre is “to hesitate to do”, most often with a negative (nōn dubitō, “I don’t hesitate to”) or in a question (quid dubitās?, “why are you hesitating?”). Its other sense, “to doubt”, is in doubt. sine dubitātiōne is “without hesitation”.

Other words

  • cūnctor, cūnctārī, cūnctātus sum — hesitate, hang back, delay

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 10.8.5: assequor omnia sī properō, sī cūnctor āmittō (Lewis & Short); Liv. 2.10.9

    To be slow to act, from caution or reluctance: Fabius was Cūnctātor. The noun is cūnctātiō (Cic. Amic. 44).

  • haesitō, haesitāre, haesitāvī, haesitātum — hesitate, be at a loss; falter in speech

    verb, first conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.52: dubitant, haesitant, revocant sē interdum (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 1.115: linguā haesitantēs (Lewis & Short)

    Properly “to stick fast” (see stuck); then to be stuck for what to do or say, uncertain, at a loss.

Examples

  • nec vērō dubitat agricola, quamvīs sit senex, quaerentī cui serat respondēre: ‘dīs immortālibus’

    nor does the farmer, old as he is, hesitate to answer anyone who asks whom he is planting for: ‘for the immortal gods’Cic. Sen. 25

  • cūnctātī aliquamdiū sunt, dum alius alium, ut proelium incipiant, circumspectant

    they hung back for a while, each looking round at the others to start the fightLiv. 2.10.9

  • studium semper adsit, cūnctātiō absit

    let there always be eagerness, and no hanging backCic. Amic. 44

  • quid dubitāmus pultāre atque hūc ēvocāre ambōs forās?

    why are we hesitating to knock and call them both out here?Plaut. Bacch. 5.1.29 (Lewis & Short)

See also doubt, stuck.

SourcesLewis & Short: dubito · Lewis & Short: cunctor · Lewis & Short: haesito

Cicero (Sen. 25, Amic. 44) and Livy from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-livius); the other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
